title: Sort
description: A summer photograph of a level crossing with one wave of it pixel-sorted: the verge is combed into hard one-pixel strips that run along the ground, rise past the poles and lift the grass off the ground in one curling surface, its tips breaking pale where the sky and the walls are pushed out to the crest, while every pole and sign stays untouched. Brush anywhere and the picture sorts under your hand, live on the GPU; the longer and harder you brush, the longer the spans grow. Press and hold and the sort runs backwards, every pixel sliding home.
intent: After Kim Asendorf's ASDF Pixel Sort (2010, https://github.com/kimasendorf/ASDFPixelSort) and herb's generative reference 2 (a street photo smeared into strips that curl up like grass). A real sort at the print's full 2400x1600: spans may only start on grass and run on, within a reach and an ASDF luminance interval that both grow with the brush, ending once they have run 15% of their reach through anything but vegetation, or at a silhouette in the depth map (Depth Anything V2) or a depth step, so they never cross a pole; sorted greenest and darkest first (luminance minus greenness) by odd-even transposition in WebGL2 fragment passes along a curl-shaped family of sort lines; outside a span the same network orders pixels by home index, so erasing the mask sorts every pixel back home.

sources.author: XS Xue (@xxs11)
sources.note: 6000x4000 original, shown at 2400x1600; depth from Depth Anything V2 Small via tools/depth/depth_hr.py, 1200x800.
